title: DB round-trip counting proxy
summary: CountingConnection/CountingCursor wrapping the pool — the single custom primitive that makes SDK-internal round-trip fan-out (dedup, ingest-resolver, multi-type search, context-card) countably measurable and CI-gateable, independent of runner speed.
description:
Build `benchmarks/common/counting.py`: a `CountingConnection`/`CountingCursor` pair wrapping the `ConnectionPool`'s raw `ibm_db` handles, exposing per-SDK-call `execute`/`fetch` counts via a `round_trips` pytest fixture and an `assert_round_trips(n)` helper. This is the highest-value custom piece BENCHMARK_STRATEGY.md identifies — nothing off the shelf knows what constitutes "one SDK call," and this is the only metric in the whole strategy that is genuinely immune to GHA runner-speed noise, which is why Tier 1 (EPIC-17's BM-20) gates PRs on it instead of on wall-clock. Makes A3 (dedup pre-SELECT), A7 (ingest-resolver pre-search), B9 (multi-type fan-out), and B11 (context-card composite) countably measurable for the first time.

Acceptance: counts verified against known-shape operations (e.g. `get_by_id()` must count exactly 1); zero measurable overhead when the proxy is disabled (benchmarked against a direct-pool baseline); works transparently across all 5 repositories plus the shared chunk repo; covered by its own unit tests, not just used inside benchmarks. Depends on BM-3.
